title: Trebbiano
description: Also called Ugni Blanc in France. A neutral, high-acid grape behind Cognac, Armagnac and Vin Santo.
L: Explain why it's so widely planted

Trebbiano, called Ugni Blanc in France, gives light, crisp whites with lemon, green apple, almond and herbs. It has high acidity and moderate alcohol, and is fairly neutral in aroma. It's one of the most planted white grapes in the world, mostly for brandy and simple wines.

Trebbiano is vigorous, productive and resistant to disease, and keeps high acidity even when yields are high. That makes it ideal for distillation, where neutral, acidic, low-alcohol wine is needed. Its many clones and relatives, like Trebbiano Toscano and Trebbiano Romagnolo, share the family name.
Why is Trebbiano valued for brandy?
It gives neutral, acidic, low-alcohol wine
Distillers want neutral, acidic base wine.

As a still wine, Trebbiano is pale, light, crisp and neutral, with lemon and almond. It's often blended to add freshness. Trebbiano d'Abruzzo, a distinct variety, can be more serious, especially from top producers like Valentini.
Trebbiano is a low-yielding, delicate grape.
Not true. It's vigorous and productive.
Trebbiano gives light, crisp, neutral whites
It's productive and keeps high acidity
It's one of the most planted white grapes
Explain its role in French brandy

Trebbiano grows across central Italy. Trebbiano Toscano is used in Tuscany, Umbria and Lazio, often in blends like Orvieto and Frascati, and in Vin Santo. Trebbiano Romagnolo grows in Emilia-Romagna. Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is a separate variety. Lugana, near Lake Garda, uses Turbiana, once called Trebbiano di Lugana.

In France, Ugni Blanc is the main grape of Cognac, about 98% of plantings there, and Armagnac. In the south, it's used in Côtes de Gascogne IGP whites, often blended with Colombard. Local names include Saint-Émilion in Charente, unrelated to the Bordeaux village.
Match each name to its place.
The Trebbiano family has many members.
In Cognac, Ugni Blanc's local name is Saint-Émilion. Don't confuse it with the Bordeaux appellation.
Which wines or spirits use Trebbiano or Ugni Blanc?
Trebbiano grows across central Italy in several varieties
Ugni Blanc is about 98% of Cognac
It's used in Gascony whites and Armagnac
From thin wine to great brandy
Explain why Cognac uses Ugni Blanc

Cognac's base wine is made from Ugni Blanc picked early, at about 8 to 9% alcohol, with very high acidity. It's thin and sour to drink, but ideal for distillation: high acidity keeps it stable without added sulphur, which producers avoid because it would taint the spirit, and neutrality lets distillation and oak shape the spirit.

Cognac is distilled twice in copper pot stills, called alembic charentais. The first distillation gives brouillis, about 28 to 32%. The second gives the heart, la bonne chauffe, around 70%. It then ages in French oak, from Limousin or Tronçais, for years. Distillation must be finished by 31 March after harvest.
The thin wine is distilled twice, then aged.

Cognac is labelled by minimum age: VS, at least 2 years in oak; VSOP, at least 4 years; XO, at least 10 years since 2018. Cognac's crus, like Grande Champagne and Petite Champagne, on chalk, give the finest spirits. Armagnac, in Gascony, uses Ugni Blanc too, often with single, column distillation.
What is the minimum oak age for XO Cognac since 2018?
XO was raised from 6 to 10 years in 2018.
Cognac uses thin, acidic Ugni Blanc wine
It's distilled twice in copper pot stills
VS, VSOP and XO mark minimum ages
Explain how Vin Santo is made

Vin Santo, holy wine, is a Tuscan sweet wine made mainly from Trebbiano and Malvasia. Grapes are dried on straw mats or hung from rafters for months, until Christmas or later, concentrating sugar. They're pressed into a thick, sweet must, then sealed into small barrels.

The must ferments slowly in small barrels called caratelli, often 50 to 100 litres, sealed for three to five years or more. Traditionally they're kept in attics, through hot summers and cold winters. Some caratelli keep a madre, mother, a deposit of old yeast and wine, which starts fermentation. The wine oxidises slowly, becoming amber.
What is a madre in Vin Santo?
A deposit of old yeast and wine left in the barrel
The madre helps start fermentation and adds character.

Vin Santo ranges from dry to very sweet, amber to brown, with nuts, dried apricot, caramel, honey and a slightly oxidised note. Vin Santo del Chianti Classico and di Montepulciano are DOCs. Occhio di Pernice, partridge's eye, is a rare version made from Sangiovese.
Amber, nutty, from dry to sweet
Vin Santo is always made from red grapes.
Not true. It's mainly Trebbiano and Malvasia; only Occhio di Pernice uses Sangiovese.
Vin Santo is made from dried Trebbiano and Malvasia
It ages for years in small sealed caratelli
It's amber, nutty and from dry to sweet

Dry Trebbiano suits light, simple food: salads, grilled fish, seafood pasta, fried food and antipasti. Its acidity and neutrality make it refreshing. Lugana, from Turbiana, suits lake fish. Trebbiano d'Abruzzo from top producers suits richer fish and white meat.
In Tuscany, Vin Santo is served with cantucci, almond biscuits, dipped into the glass. It also suits blue cheese, nut tarts and dried fruit. Serve at 12 to 14 degrees. It keeps for weeks once opened.
Which Tuscan biscuits are traditionally dipped in Vin Santo?
Almond cantucci are the classic match.
Serve dry Trebbiano well chilled and young. Its charm is freshness, not complexity.
Dry Trebbiano suits light seafood and antipasti
Vin Santo suits cantucci, blue cheese and nut tarts
Drink dry Trebbiano young; Vin Santo keeps
